podcast.body: Six years after "Johnny B. Good" was released, Carl Wilson of The Beach Boys used the instantly recognizable guitar introduction from Chuck Berry's song as the intro to "Fun Fun Fun." This demonstrates how Berry's slight twist on a standard riff had made it uniquely identifiable with him. "When six years later Carl Wilson of the Beach Boys played this as the intro to Fun Fun Fun. Absolutely no one listening thought, oh he's riffing off Texas Shout by Cal Cal Davenport. Everyone instantly thought, oh that's the intro to Johnny Be Good."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
srcs.episode: Episode 67: "Johnny B. Goode", by Chuck Berry

podcast.body: Recorded on January 1, 1964, this song fused two of Brian Wilson's key influences. It features Mike Love's witty lyrics and an opening intro directly borrowed from Chuck Berry's "Johnny B. Good". While maintaining a Chuck Berry feel overall, the verse adopts a distinct harmonic direction, utilizing a 1-4-1-5 progression reminiscent of The Ronettes' "Be My Baby," though applied to a different effect. It became the group's fourth top 10 hit, reaching number five on the charts, despite intense competition from The Beatles. "Fun, fun, fun, have lyrics by Mike Love, saw of his wittiest, and start out with an intro taken straight from Johnny B. Good."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
